checks.diff_scope: One file, two symmetric hunks in getLoopTripCount. Each hunk is an isPhysical() branch that accepts only when checkForImmediate succeeds ($x0 = 0) and returns nullptr otherwise. The virtual-register branch is textually unchanged. No removed logic, no stubs, no test edits. The new early return is a real bail-out: a physical register other than x0 has no SSA def and no known value at the preheader. This matches HexagonHardwareLoops::checkForImmediate at llvmorg-20.1.8 (line 1550: '!R.isVirtual() -> return false'), whose getLoopTripCount would likewise refuse the loop. The InitialValue hunk is effectively dead, because PHI operands are always virtual, but it is harmless and symmetric.
checks.trip_count_bne_beq: GVSoC, llc -filetype=obj from shapes.ll, driver built by GAP9 GCC, n = 0,1,2,3,7,100. 'BNE %iv.next,$x0 -> header' (ne0) and 'BEQ %iv.next,$x0 -> exit' (eq0exit) give exactly n iterations, and 0 when the zero-trip guard skips the loop. Both match the GCC-compiled C reference. computeCount's path is: COPY $x0 into a vreg, swap because IVBump<0, start==0, count=End=n. That is correct for these two orientations.

checks.fuzzer: benchmarks/hwloop-fuzz gen.py seeds 1..160, one.sh adapted to base=int-20 and new=20-F003, both simulated against the GAP9 GCC -O2 checksum (logs/20-F003-review/one.sh, res.txt). O2: int-20 crashes in PULP Hardware Loops on 108/160. F003 on those: 53 OK, 44 MISMATCH, 2 HANG, 9 FAIL (asserts in 'PULP Hardware Loop Fixup'). The 43 int-20-OK programs stay OK, and the 9 int-20 MISMATCH stay MISMATCH (pre-existing). O3: crashes 107/160, then 70 OK, 23 MISMATCH, 14 FAIL, and 46 OK->OK. Os: crashes 110/160, then 99 OK, 1 MISMATCH, 10 FAIL, and 46 OK->OK. No program that int-20 compiled and ran correctly is broken by F003 (0 regressions). Attribution (logs/20-F003-review/combo.sh, combo.txt): the IR is compiled with F003 llc up to riscv-expand-pseudo, i.e. through F003's hwloop pass, then finished with either F003 llc or F005 llc (F005 contains the Fixup layout fix). Of 122 non-OK F003 cases, the F003 finish reproduces the failure and the F005 finish gives the GCC result in 120 (80 MISMATCH->OK, 38 FAIL->OK, 2 HANG->OK). The remaining 2 (seed 27 O2/O3) are a structural defect: tail duplication leaves two lp.setup in two predecessors of the same loop with different end labels. The trip counts in that code are correct (m, n+1, n). So F003's counts are right; the wrong results come from the Fixup/layout stage.

findings_not_blocking: OPEN, pre-existing defect newly reachable through $x0 (recommend a separate task before relying on hwloops for arbitrary IR): computeCount ignores the comparison kind and the branch direction in its register path. The fork dropped HexagonHardwareLoops' 'Negated = ... ^ (TB != Header)' and its equality adjustment (fork FIXME 'AdjV'). Hand-written IR then miscounts on GVSoC (logs/20-F003-review/shapes.ll). (a) eqm: 'icmp eq %i.next, %m' continue-when-equal. LSR turns it into 'BEQ %iv, $x0 -> header'. F003 forms lp.setup with count n-m (n=100: 100 iterations, correct is 1). int-20 crashes on it. (b) ge0: 'icmp sgt %i.next, -1' giving 'BGE %iv.next, $x0 -> header'. F003 counts n, correct is n+1. int-20 crashes on it. The same miscount exists today for virtual-register bounds: gem, 'icmp sge %i.next, %m', gets count n-m instead of n-m+1 on int-20 and ref-18. clang -O2 from C did not produce these shapes in any test (instcombine canonicalises them; loops5.c and the 160-seed fuzzer found no F003 trip-count error). The note's claim that computeCount 'already handled this case' holds only for NE->header / EQ->exit.

Pre-existing, unrelated to F003 (identical asm on int-20 and ref-18): unguarded do/while loops get no zero/negative-trip guard, because loopCountMayWrapOrUnderFlow is commented out in computeCount. 'do{}while(--i>=0)' with n=-5 hangs (count n+1<=0). '(i-=2)>=0' is off by one, and '++i<m' with n>m hangs.
Pre-existing: Fixup layout defects (F005's task). F003 exposes many more loops to them, hence the landing condition.
Observation: GAP9 GCC 7.1.1 -O2 miscompiles 'do{c++;}while(--i>0)' (returns 1 for n=2..100). GCC checksums are not an infallible oracle. The fuzzer and FIR checks above still agree with GCC.
